chapter: California, Art Tatum and Lionel Hampton
title: Nat King Cole recommends him to Hampton; writing for a parade band
summary: Hampton wanted Cole's trio, Cole refused and recommended Thompson; the two wrote music for a Local 767 street parade band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: And who was in Hamp's band?
There was quite a number of musicians.

Well, first of all as I said, number one, the main reason why I was recommended to Lionel was because Lionel had made some very famous records with King Cole, specifically 'Jack the Bellboy' and a couple other things which were really terrific hits. And he wanted King Cole to

play with him, and his entire trio as part of the rhythm section. But King Cole refused to give up his musician because he had faith in himself. And it was through the recommendation of King Cole, who knew about my ability, that he recommended me to Lionel Hampton.

In fact, another thing that happened during that time. They had a street parade once with bands, bands that participated in a street parade including Jimmy Lumsford and some other band. I think it was a band, it might have been organized by the musician's union, 767. But it was like two bands playing together. And King Cole and I were contracted to write the music for this arrangements for this band, and that's how King Cole and I became close in writing this music and going around jamming at night. I learned a lot from King Cole too.
